extracted.intended_audience: Researchers / Principal Investigators applying for ERC Advanced Grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applicants and reviewers on how ERC Advanced Grant proposals are evaluated: excellence as the sole criterion, assessed through two main elements (the research project and the principal investigator) with specified sub‑dimensions and track record expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence (primary and sole evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by selected international peer reviewers who assess them on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All assessment and marking at each evaluation step must be based solely on 'excellence' — there are no other independent primary criteria. Reviewers should judge proposals against the standard of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground‑breaking nature (research project)
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the proposed research is ground‑breaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ERC panels primarily evaluate the ground‑breaking nature of the research project; this refers to novelty, potential to open new directions, and to challenge existing paradigms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition (research project)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ambition of the proposed research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambition indicates the scale, scope and daring of the scientific objectives — high‑risk/high‑gain approaches are part of what ERC seeks to support if justified by excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility (research project)
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility of the proposed research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where highly ambitious or ground‑breaking, the project must be feasible: reviewers assess whether the proposed work can realistically be carried out given the described approach, resources and timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual capacity (principal investigator)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellectual capacity of the applicant principal investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess the PI's intellectual ability to conceive and drive the proposed research, evidenced through past achievements and demonstrated leadership in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity (principal investigator)
rubrics_metrics.description: The creativity of the applicant principal investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the PI's originality and ability to generate transformative ideas and novel approaches; creativity is a key characteristic sought for successful execution of ground‑breaking projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment (principal investigator)
rubrics_metrics.description: The commitment of the applicant principal investigator to the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether the PI is sufficiently committed (time, leadership, and focus) to lead and deliver the proposed research successfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal investigator profile / track record (10‑year window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be exceptional leaders in terms of originality and significance of research with an excellent track record and achievements during the last 10 years (this time window can be extended in case of eligible career breaks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of an excellent track record may include: significant research output (e.g., publications, monographs, books); notable invitations to international conferences as keynote speaker; significant inventions, patents; recognition through major prizes and awards; major leadership/membership of established research institutions. The 10‑year window may be extended for eligible career breaks — reviewers should take such adjustments into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation step outcomes (step 1 result categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of step 1 of the evaluation, applicants are informed that their proposal is: [A] of sufficient quality to pass to step 2; [B] of high quality but not sufficient to pass to step 2; or [C] not of sufficient quality to pass to step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcome labels communicate whether the proposal advances to the next evaluation step. They summarize reviewers' combined judgments on the research project and PI against the excellence standard.
